Cusco · Perú

Maras Salt Ponds

Salt harvest and spring-fed evaporation ponds

Current ratingsOpening hoursView the place on the map
Nearby places

Explore

Salty springwater is distributed among small evaporation ponds worked by local families. From the visitor side, look at how the water is divided before it reaches a basin. Different colours can reflect water depth and stages of evaporation, not different kinds of stone.

Planning your visit

45–75 min · Allow this time for the visit itself. Add travel, admission queues and any scheduled tour separately.

What to look for

Salt harvest and spring-fed evaporation ponds

Use the public lookout to frame a group of ponds with different water levels. Their small feeder channels are often a more informative detail than the broad white panorama.

History and local experience

Salt is harvested rather than quarried from these ponds. Watching the entry channel and the exposed crystals links the landscape to an ongoing local livelihood.

Walking route

  1. Salineras de Maras, comunidad de Maras, Urubamba
  2. Use the community visitor entrance, walk to the authorised viewing terrace and follow a feeder channel with your eyes.
  3. Stay outside the working pans to protect the salt harvest.
